observations: The gate is exactly upstream's: legacy iff t < kRecyclableFullType (5) or t == kSetCompressionType (9). The binary implements it as two compares (cmp $4, jle; cmp $9, jne recyclable), so types 10..15 and negative types also take the recyclable arm -- see unknowns for the out-of-range seed read.

The CRC chain is Value + Combine, not a single Extend: payload_crc = Extend(0, ptr, n) (== Value), then Crc32cCombine(seed, payload_crc, n). The combine identity makes this equal to a direct Extend over (type byte [+ log_number] + payload); all 600 crc_combine cases pin the equality, and the 100 combine-identity binding rows re-verify it.

The seed load precedes the gate (0x5f03bc0 before 0x5f03bc5): type_crc_[type] is read even when the recyclable arm then extends it. The recyclable extension reads buf+7 (the just-stored log_number bytes at rsp+0x44), not the Writer field directly.
Mask is ror(crc, 15) + 0xa282ead8: the binary does ror $0xf then sub $0x5d7d1528, and 0x5d7d1528 == -0xa282ead8 mod 2^32. Unmask (rol 15 after subtracting the delta) round-trips in every case.

Length truncation: the upstream assert(n <= 0xffff) is compiled out, so the header stores only the low 16 bits of the length (mov %r8w) while the CRC covers the full payload. Pinned by the two 0x10000/0x10001 header_build rows (header length 0/1, CRC over the full 64 KiB payload). AddRecord never passes more than 0x7ff9, so this is a latent quirk, not a live path.

Log-number truncation: only the low 32 bits of the 64-bit log_number_ are stored (EncodeFixed32), so two log numbers 2^32 apart produce identical recyclable headers. Pinned by the 0x100000000 / 0x123456789 log_number rows.

Append checksum args: the header Append passes crc arg 0 and the payload Append passes payload_crc -- the writer checksums the payload, not the header. This matches upstream log_writer.cc:445-451 exactly, including the 0 /* crc32c_checksum */ comment on the header call. The same three-argument Append form appears in AddRecord's trailer-padding call (crc 0).

Status move byte rules: the second Append's result is move-assigned into the sret, copying bytes 0-1, 3-4, 5, 8-15 and preserving byte 2 (sev_) and bytes 6-7 (padding) from the header status. The old header state_ is delete[]'d when non-null. The second delete[] in the epilogue (0x5f03d0b) is dead code -- its slot (rsp+0x28) was just zeroed by the move.
No Flush here: unlike AddRecord and AddCompressionTypeRecord, EmitPhysicalRecord never calls dest_->Flush(). Upstream log_writer.cc:443-457 agrees -- the Flush lives in the callers.
TEST_SYNC_POINT_CALLBACK is compiled out: no call sits between the Mask (0x5f03c01..0x5f03c0c) and the header store. The binary goes straight from the Mask to building the header Slice.

The first Append writes its result DIRECTLY into the caller's sret slot (rbp); the second writes into a 16-byte stack slot (rsp+0x20) and is then moved over it. That is why the move preserves byte 2 / bytes 6-7: they are the first Append's bytes, and the callee's error path writes bytes 0-3, 4-5, 8-15 (movl $5 / movw / movq) but never bytes 6-7.

The .cold pad is shared in shape with the sibling packets' pads (delete state_, canary check, _Unwind_Resume) but entered from a stub INSIDE the main FDE (0x5f03d1a..0x5f03d26) rather than from a stub after it; the 5 bytes 0x5f03b7b..0x5f03b80 are alignment padding.
unknowns: WritableFileWriter::Append's body (0x6054680..0x605518b, 2827 B) is not reconstructed here -- only its contract is an input. Its buffering, rate-limiter interaction, checksum-generator update, IOOptions handling and the exact meaning of the byte at this+0x89 (previous-error flag) are unpinned. Its full body is the natural follow-up packet.

Types outside 0..9 (10..15, negatives): the binary takes the recyclable arm and loads type_crc_[type] past the 10-entry array, reading manual_flush_/compression_type_/compress_ bytes as the CRC seed. The gate decision is pinned (bindings rows for types 0..15); the out-of-range seed value is NOT modelled -- cases use types 0..9 only.

Whether the returned status's bytes 6-7 (padding, never written by the Append callee's error path) ever matter to a caller: both callers (AddRecord, AddCompressionTypeRecord) move the 16-byte status in their frames right after the call; whether bytes 6-7 are read was not traced.
The exact .cold entry-point selection (which exception region uses the stub at 0x5f03d1a): the stub and the pad are pinned, but the LSDA region mapping was not decoded.
